question: 400 pears were bought at ₹1250 per hundred and were sold at a profit of ₹900. Find the selling price (in ₹) per dozen of pears.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total CP of 400 pears = 4 × 1250 = ₹5000

Total SP of 400 pears = 5000 + 900 = ₹5900

SP of 1 pear = 5900 ÷ 400 = 59/4

SP of 1 dozen (12 pears) = (59/4) × 12 = 59 × 3 = 177

**∴ The correct answer is ₹177.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of pears bought = 400

Rate of purchase = ₹1250 per 100 pears

Total profit earned = ₹900

**Formula Used:**

Total SP = Total CP + Profit

SP per dozen = (Total SP ÷ Total Quantity) × 12

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total CP = 4 × 1250 = ₹5000

⇒ Total SP = Total CP + Profit

⇒ Total SP = 5000 + 900 = ₹5900

⇒ SP of 1 pear = 5900 ÷ 400 = 59/4

⇒ SP per dozen = (59/4) × 12 = 59 × 3 = ₹177

**∴ The correct answer is ₹177.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit & Loss Percentage

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 | Loss % = (Loss ÷ CP) × 100. Profit and loss are always calculated on Cost Price (CP) unless specified.

Unitary Method for Pricing

To find the cost of a specific quantity (like a dozen), calculate the cost of a single unit first: Price of 1 Unit = Total Price ÷ Total Quantity.

Marked Price & Discount

Selling Price (SP) = Marked Price (MP) − Discount. Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price.
